entry.title: Port of Los Angeles Foils 120 Million Cyberattacks in August
entry.content:
Links: ft.com | news.bgov.com

The Port of Los Angeles reported thwarting more than 120 million cyberattack attempts in August alone, nearly doubling its monthly average from 2023. These threats included network exploitation, credential harvesting, malware, and intrusion attempts. As a primary hub for crude oil exports, the port's escalating risk highlights a growing vulnerability in critical maritime infrastructure to sophisticated cyber warfare.

Port Executive Director Gene Seroka provided the data, contrasting the August surge with a 2023 baseline of approximately 63 million monthly intrusions. To counter these threats, the port established a Cyber Resilience Center in 2022. The incident underscores the intensifying pressure on shipping companies to secure complex supply chains against persistent, high-volume digital attacks.

entry.title: FBI Issues Warning on ARTEX AI Hacking Framework
entry.content:
Links: 404media.co | ic3.gov

ARTEX is an open-source framework that utilizes agentic AI to automate cyberattacks at "machine speed." By connecting to various large language models, the tool deploys multiple agents to perform tasks ranging from infrastructure reconnaissance to full-scale data theft. The FBI issued a warning in November 2026 stating that malicious actors are using ARTEX to target global sectors, including government, healthcare, defense, finance, and semiconductors.

Although the original creator moved the tool to a closed-source model, the code remains widely accessible through various forks and public repositories. Security experts note that the framework reduces the time required for complex manual hacking tasks from days to just a few hours. While it poses a significant threat for espionage, the tool is also being used by security teams for authorized penetration testing and bug bounty research.

entry.title: Aerogramme Improves Concurrent Mailbox Access in Distributed IMAP Server
entry.content:
Links: aerogramme.deuxfleurs.fr | lobsters

Aerogramme, a geo-distributed email server, is refining its IMAP implementation to handle concurrent mailbox access reliably. The project addresses the technical difficulty of maintaining data consistency when multiple clients or multiple server nodes access the same mailbox simultaneously. Key focus areas include ensuring the monotonicity of UIDVALIDITY and managing legacy IMAP behaviors regarding message sequence numbers.

The development team redesigned Aerogramme's mailbox state interface to separate local client views from remote storage synchronization. This approach allows for sequential reasoning about mailbox operations within a single connection while explicitly managing synchronization with the distributed backend. The implementation utilizes a convergent operation log and the Garage K2V key-value store to provide consistency without relying on distributed locks or transactions.

entry.title: Security Risks Identified in AI-Powered Self-Healing Code
entry.content:
Links: gynvael.coldwind.pl | github.com | lobsters

Wolverine is a tool designed to give Python scripts self-healing capabilities by utilizing GPT-4 to diagnose and repair runtime errors. The system automatically captures error messages from crashing scripts, sends them to the LLM for a solution, and applies the suggested code changes to continue execution automatically.

The author highlights a critical security vulnerability where malicious user input can trigger error messages that function as prompt injections. In such cases, GPT-4 might execute unauthorized commands, such as downloading and running remote scripts, effectively weaponizing the self-healing mechanism. The author advises against deploying these tools in production environments due to these risks and the potential for unpredictable code execution.

entry.title: GitHub Implements Default Blocks on Dangerous Actions Triggers
entry.content:
Links: pyfound.blogspot.com | alpha-omega.dev | lobsters | hacker news

GitHub will start blocking the pull_request_target trigger by default in public repositories on December 2, 2026. This change addresses vulnerabilities where triggers such as pull_request_target and issue_comment allow external actors to execute workflows with access to repository secrets, a vulnerability referred to as a "pwn request." Organizations can manage these risks by implementing event policies to restrict or disable specific triggers across all repositories.

The Python Software Foundation (PSF) has already applied these security policies to its stewarded organizations to mitigate supply chain compromises similar to those seen in the Ultralytics and LiteLLM incidents. Maintainers are encouraged to use "Evaluate mode" to audit existing workflows before enforcing these policies to ensure that legitimate automated tasks, like labeling pull requests from forks, remain functional.

entry.title: Ghostscript CVE-2026-125396 Allows Remote Code Execution via Font Loader
entry.content:
Links: pwn.ai | lobsters

Researchers at pwn.ai have identified a use-after-free vulnerability (CVE-2026-125396) in Ghostscript’s Type 1 font loader. The flaw provides a write-what-where primitive in native memory, allowing an attacker to bypass the -dSAFER sandbox and achieve remote command execution. The exploit is triggered by delivering a specially crafted document to an application that passes the file to the Ghostscript interpreter for rendering.

The research demonstrates that common image processing tasks—such as cropping images or generating previews in PHP (Imagick), Python (Pillow, imageio), and Qt—can reach the vulnerable interpreter. Even if an application does not call Ghostscript directly, its underlying dependencies may do so when processing PostScript or PDF content disguised as other file types. The vulnerability stems from a failure to check operand types in a font loading helper, which, combined with a memory management error where a global dictionary retains a reference to a reclaimed local object, leads to arbitrary memory corruption.

The experiment revealed that user prompts and sensitive credentials leaked extensively due to front-door compromises at hosting providers, aggressive logging by low-cost resellers, and unauthorized scraping by third-party labs.

entry.content:

GnuPG has released GPGME version 2.3.1 to address a critical double-free vulnerability, designated CVE-2026-129975, that affects all prior versions. Discovered by Johan Carlsson, the bug can be triggered by an OpenPGP key containing a crafted, exceptionally long user ID, potentially allowing data exfiltration or remote code execution.

Because GPGME is widely utilized as a shared library across mail clients, XMPP clients, Samba, Flatpak, and related tools, the developers strongly advise an immediate update. In addition to updating the GPGME library, GnuPG has released Gpg4win version 5.1.2 and provided patches for administrators unable to upgrade immediately.

entry.title: Enroute Scales Git Infrastructure to 300,000 Repositories by Replacing Multi-Raft
entry.content:
Links: enroute.sh | lobsters

Enroute has transitioned its Git infrastructure from a Multi-Raft architecture to a hybrid system using a Raft-based root log and Vertical Paxos-inspired shard logs. This change addresses the performance bottlenecks and operational complexity caused by managing per-repository leader elections and heartbeats as repository counts scale. In the new architecture, the root log manages node membership and appoints sequencers for individual shard logs, which maintain the actual repository state and replication.

Benchmarking revealed that the new design maintains a 99th percentile push latency of 47 ms across 100,000 repositories, significantly outperforming the previous system. The team validated the new consensus protocol using Stateright for formal model checking and Jepsen for fault injection. Future plans include developing a continuous placement driver for proactive load balancing, implementing root log learners to maintain commit efficiency, and adding point-in-time restoration capabilities.

entry.title: PostgreSQL 19 Released
entry.content:
Links: postgresql.org | lobsters | hacker news

The PostgreSQL Global Development Group has released PostgreSQL 19, introducing features aimed at scaling mission-critical workloads and simplifying database administration. Key updates include the REPACK (CONCURRENTLY) command for non-disruptive table bloat cleanup, the pg_plan_advice extension for query plan stability, and "read-your-writes" consistency support on standby servers via the WAIT FOR LSN command.

The release also enhances autovacuum efficiency through parallel workers and a prioritization scoring system, streamlines logical replication initialization, and adds replication support for sequence values. Furthermore, PostgreSQL 19 introduces server-side Server Name Indication (SNI) support for TLS certificates, disables JIT compilation by default, and sets LZ4 as the default TOAST compression method.

entry.title: Running 15 Million Web Servers on a Single Virtual Machine
entry.content:
Links: kapteko.com | lobsters | hacker news

This article explores the technical feasibility of running 15 million web servers on a single virtual machine configured with 10 gigabytes of RAM and one CPU core. It examines standard operating system limitations, including port allocation ranges and per-socket memory overhead, that prevent naive implementations from scaling.

To bypass kernel-level constraints, the author proposes a custom userland runtime utilizing the smoltcp TCP/IP stack alongside high-performance networking interfaces like DPDK and AF_XDP. This design minimizes memory overhead per connection to achieve massive scale within strict hardware boundaries.

entry.title: Zerodha Introduces Blobasaur Distributed Blob Storage on SQLite
entry.content:
Links: zerodha.tech | lobsters | hacker news

Zerodha has developed Blobasaur, a sharded and distributed blob storage server written in Rust that uses SQLite as its underlying storage engine and speaks the Redis protocol. Built to replace SSDB on its trading platform Kite, Blobasaur manages high-throughput read and write operations for user workspace preferences, layouts, and interface metadata ranging from a few kilobytes to several megabytes.

The system achieves single-digit millisecond latency and handles thousands of requests per second on commodity hardware by partitioning data across multiple SQLite shards using consistent hashing. It incorporates zstd compression, group commits, and Redis Cluster protocol compatibility, allowing the engineering team to scale horizontally while maintaining operational simplicity.
